channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: A próxima medida cara de pau do governo Lula
item.description: The Lula government announced a provisional measure to mitigate rising gasoline prices, just one day after Petrobras signaled a forthcoming increase. The move follows the repeal of a tax on 'blusinhas' (cheap clothing) that the government itself had introduced, drawing criticism for policy inconsistency.

item.title: Caiado promete enquadrar facções como terroristas no 1º dia de governo
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) announced that, if elected, he would classify criminal organizations as terrorist groups on his first day in office and deploy the Armed Forces to combat organized crime. The statement was made on social media on March 13, 2025. Caiado aims to position himself as a hardline candidate on public security.

item.title: MPT abre investigação para apurar fala de Zema sobre trabalho infantil
item.description: The Labor Public Ministry (MPT) has opened an investigation against former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) over statements suggesting the expansion of work opportunities for children. The probe was initiated following a complaint by the Parliamentary Front for Combating Child Labor after Zema said in an interview that 'every child can help with simple tasks'. Although he later revised his stance to focus on adolescents and apprenticeship programs, the original remarks sparked widespread backlash.

item.title: Ao vivo: governo anuncia novas medidas para combustíveis
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announces new measures to mitigate the impact of war on Brazil's fuel sector. The announcement takes place at 3 p.m. at the Ministry of Mines and Energy, with the presence of Ministers Alexandre Silveira (Mines and Energy), Bruno Moretti (Planning and Budget), and Executive Secretary of Finance, Rogério Ceron.

item.title: Após reunião com Fachin, Flávio Bolsonaro promete ‘bonança’ entre instituições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro met with Supreme Court Minister Edson Fachin to promote institutional dialogue and prevent rumors about him, stating he seeks peace to focus on Brazil’s problems. He said that if elected, there will be a period of 'bonanza' between institutions, with mutual respect for each branch’s sphere. While praising Fachin as balanced, he maintained harsh criticism of Minister Alexandre de Moraes, accusing him of persecuting his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz acreditar na inocência de Ciro Nogueira ‘até que se prove o contrário’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) said he believes in the innocence of Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) until proven otherwise, noting that Nogueira, a former Minister of Civil House, has a fair rapporteur at the Supreme Court and a chance to defend himself. The Federal Police accused Nogueira of receiving improper benefits from banker Daniel Vorcaro in exchange for congressional assistance, including monthly payments, corporate acquisitions, international trips, and use of a property. Flávio also denied any involvement of his campaign’s communications coordinator, Marcello Lopes, with Banco Master, calling the claim a lie.

item.title: Flávio se reúne com Fachin no STF: “Fiquei com excelente impressão dele”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) met with Minister Edson Fachin, president of the STF, in an institutional meeting. He said he was left with an 'excellent impression' of the magistrate and emphasized that he requested the visit.

item.title: Perfil feminino para vice de Flávio Bolsonaro perde força no PL
item.description: The profile of a woman for Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket has lost strength within the PL, despite initially being seen as ideal by party president Valdemar Costa Neto. The campaign now prioritizes urgently attracting a Centrão party to the base, increasing the likelihood of a male vice-presidential pick. Senator Teresa Cristina (PP-MS) remains viewed as the ideal choice for the vice-presidential slot, even as the focus shifts.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro se reúne com Fachin e fala em ser mais propositivo e não reagir a provocações
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) met with Supreme Court President Minister Edson Fachin in Brasília for an institutional visit. He stated he aimed to present himself as a pre-candidate for president with a centrist, proactive profile, avoiding reactions to provocations and emphasizing respect for institutions and a forward-looking approach. Flávio denied discussing dosimetry or any ongoing STF rulings, describing the meeting as amicable and focused on pleasantries.

item.title: Pacheco reforça ao PT que não será candidato ao governo de Minas Gerais
item.description: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB) informed PT leader Edinho Silva that he will not run for governor of Minas Gerais in 2026, citing personal reasons and a possible exit from politics after his term. However, PT militants in the state still hope President Lula will convince him to run, especially after Pacheco suggested two alternatives: Josué Gomes and Jarbas Soares. The decision is not seen as final, as Edinho Silva plans to revisit the conversation with Pacheco.

item.title: Reação de Lula reforça leve favoritismo na eleição
item.description: Lula remains in a technical tie with Flávio Bolsonaro in second-round simulations, but his approval rating has stopped declining and shown signs of recovery, particularly following recent government actions. Despite persistent headwinds like inflation and indebtedness, measures such as repealing the 'blusinhas' tax, fighting organized crime, debt renegotiation, and diesel subsidies have strengthened his position. The outlook suggests a slight advantage for Lula, though the outcome may hinge on factors beyond his control, such as ongoing investigations.

item.title: Presidente do PT no Rio posa com arma e camiseta de Lula
item.description: The president of the PT in Rio de Janeiro, Diego Zeidan Quaquá, posted a photo holding a rifle at a shooting range while wearing a Lula-branded shirt, declaring himself a follower of revolutionary figures like Che Guevara and Marighella. The image was later deleted after public backlash. He is the son of Maricá’s mayor and national PT vice-president Washington Quaquá, who faced criticism within the party for defending the innocence of the Brazão brothers, later convicted in the murder of Marielle Franco.

item.title: Ao vivo: STF julga igualdade salarial e alcance da Maria da Penha
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court is ruling on Wednesday on the constitutionality of Law 14.611/2023, which requires companies with 100 or more employees to disclose salary reports and remuneration criteria to ensure gender pay equality. The Court will also decide whether protective measures under the Maria da Penha Law can be applied in gender-based violence cases absent a domestic, familial, or affective relationship between victim and aggressor, with general repercussion recognized.

item.title: Em aceno ao governo, Motta decide colocar em apreciação o PL do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta decided to put the bill ending the 6x1 work schedule to a vote, following the Lula government’s submission of the proposal with constitutional urgency. Initially viewed with skepticism by opposition-aligned lawmakers as an attempt by Lula to claim ownership of an idea already under legislative discussion as a PEC, the bill will now proceed in parallel with the constitutional amendment, deemed complementary to align legislation with forthcoming constitutional changes.

item.title: Explosão causada pela Sabesp vira munição eleitoral para Haddad em SP
item.description: A gas explosion caused by Sabesp in Jaguaré, which left one dead and three injured, was used by Fernando Haddad as electoral ammunition against Tarcísio de Freitas’ government, linking Sabesp’s privatization to rising tariffs, complaints, and profits. Haddad claimed privatization benefited only buyers while the public bore the costs, citing unfulfilled promises of lower tariffs. Governor Tarcísio called an emergency meeting and pledged compensation and accountability, while PT lawmakers condemned privatization as a Bolsonarist legacy harming the people.

item.title: O acordo de Motta com o governo para votar a PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta announced that the House will advance the government's bill to end the 6×1 work scale, following an agreement with the Executive. The text will address sector-specific details and complement a constitutional amendment proposal (PEC) on the issue. The measure aims to reform working hours in specific sectors, with ongoing negotiations between branches of government.

item.title: Oposição apoiará fim da ‘taxa das blusinhas’ de Lula
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Chamber, Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB), announced support for the Provisional Measure that eliminates the 'blusinhas tax' of 20% on international purchases up to US$50, signed by Lula. He stated the measure results from popular pressure and opposition action, not as government support, but as a victory for the Brazilian people. The MP is valid for up to 120 days and requires congressional approval to become permanent law.

item.title: Quaest: 60% avaliam reunião de Lula e Trump como positiva
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll conducted from May 8 to 11, 2026, reveals that 60% of Brazilians view the Lula-Trump meeting at the White House positively, considering it beneficial for Brazil. 43% believe Lula emerged politically strengthened from the encounter, and 37% see a positive impact on his image. The survey also shows increased support for alignment with the U.S., rising from 43% in April to 56% after the meeting.

item.title: Democrata, ex-PMB, lança brigadeiro da reserva como pré-candidato a presidente
item.description: The Democrata party, formerly the Brazilian Women's Party (PMB), launched the presidential pre-candidacy of Brigadeiro Átila Maia on March 12, 2026, a figure associated with the military reserve. The candidacy positions itself in the center-right with a nationalist platform, aiming to capture votes in an already crowded field of ideologically similar candidates.

item.title: Real é 2ª moeda que mais se valoriza durante conflito no Oriente Médio
item.description: The Brazilian real appreciated 5.09% against the U.S. dollar since the start of the Middle East conflict on February 28, marking the second-largest gain among 27 currencies analyzed, behind only the Israeli new shekel (8.28%). This appreciation was driven by rising oil prices, which boosted exports and dollar inflows into Brazil, combined with the central bank's contractionary monetary policy that maintained high real interest rates and attracted foreign capital. The stronger real also improves public finances through increased royalty revenues.

item.title: Messias agradece presidente da OAB por fala em posse no TSE
item.description: Attorney General of the Union Jorge Messias thanked OAB President Beto Simonetti for mentioning him during the swearing-in of Minister Kassio Nunes Marques as president of the TSE on Tuesday, May 12, 2026, in Brasília. Simonetti highlighted Messias while greeting the Brazilian legal profession, which was met with applause from attendees. The ceremony took place weeks after the Senate rejected Messias’s nomination to the STF, a major political setback for President Lula’s government.

item.title: STF AO VIVO – Lei da Igualdade Salarial e ampliação da Lei Maria da Penha – sessão de 13/5/2026
item.description: The STF is set to rule on the constitutionality of the Pay Equality Law (Law 14.611/2023), which mandates salary transparency in companies with over 100 employees, as well as whether the Maria da Penha Law applies to gender-based violence outside familial or affective contexts and the inclusion of inflation adjustments in judicial deposit corrections. The court will also consider ADPF 881, seeking to prevent the criminalization of prosecutors and judges for interpretive prevarication.

item.title: Fim da “taxa das blusinhas” não melhorará popularidade de Lula, diz oposição
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Chamber of Deputies, Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB), stated that the revocation of the 'blusinhas tax' will not improve President Lula's popularity, arguing that the public will realize the same government that created the measure is now repealing it without addressing real issues.

item.title: Texto do governo Lula vai regulamentar PEC do fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: The Lula government plans to use the bill already sent to Congress to regulate the PEC that reduces the workweek and ends the 6x1 schedule, establishing transition rules and sector-specific details. The agreement with Chamber President Hugo Motta was reached on Wednesday, May 13, 2026, and the PEC is expected to reach the plenary in May, followed by the bill's approval for constitutional regulation.

item.title: CNI aposta que encontro entre Lula e Trump foi passo importante para acordo sobre tarifas
item.description: CNI President Ricardo Alban highlighted the recent meeting between Lula and Trump as a significant step toward resolving trade tariff tensions, noting the 30-day extension of U.S. trade investigations as a positive signal. He urged Brazil to adopt a pragmatic approach, focusing on adding value to industrial production rather than relying solely on commodity exports. Despite a 6.7% decline in Brazilian exports to the U.S. in 2025, Alban sees opportunities to deepen economic cooperation in industry, energy, and technology based on mutual complementarity.

item.title: Brasil não aguenta mais PowerPoint contra o crime, diz Flávio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized President Lula's Brazil Against Organized Crime program, stating that Brazil 'can't take any more PowerPoint presentations against crime'. He claimed the PT only acknowledged organized crime ahead of elections after 17 years in power, called the R$ 11 billion investment inadequate and late, and pointed to ongoing failures in combating the PCC and CV, arms smuggling via borders, and rising urban violence.

item.title: Taxa da blusinha ainda não foi removida de todos os sites, apesar de suspensão pelo governo; confira
item.description: President Lula's government suspended the 'blusinha tax' (20% Import Duty) for international purchases under US$ 50 via the Remessa Conforme program, effective this Wednesday. However, Shein and Temu have not yet updated their systems and still charge the tax, while Mercado Livre, Shopee, and AliExpress have removed it, retaining only the state ICMS tax (17%-20%) on these transactions.

item.title: Governo Lula vai anunciar MP para evitar alta na gasolina
item.description: The Lula government will announce a provisional measure to mitigate the expected gasoline price increase by Petrobras, after the state-owned company signaled an imminent adjustment. The measure arises due to the stagnation of PLP 114, which proposed using extra oil revenues to untax fuels, and follows meetings between the Ministries of Finance, Planning, Civil House, Mines and Energy, and Petrobras representatives. Petrobras president Magda Chambriard confirmed the price increase will happen 'very soon', but said government and company are working on a joint initiative to ease the impact on the population.

item.title: Republicanos pede que STF suspenda votação direta para governo de Roraima
item.description: The National Directory of the Republicans has asked the Supreme Federal Court (STF) to suspend direct elections for governor in Roraima, arguing that the vacancy occurred less than six months before the end of the term, which, according to precedent, would require an indirect election. The party contends that holding elections while the STF has not yet defined the rules for such contests is imprudent, referencing a case under the rapporteurship of Minister Cristiano Zanin that discusses the electoral model for an interim governor in Rio de Janeiro. The Republicans request that the president of the Legislative Assembly of Roraima, as the immediate successor, remain in office until the STF rules on the merits of the case.

item.title: Fachin barra novas manobras como a que impediu quebra de sigilos de empresa de Toffoli
item.description: Supreme Court President Edson Fachin blocked a procedural maneuver used by the defense of Maridt, a company linked to Minister Dias Toffoli, to force a favorable ruling from Minister Gilmar Mendes on the annulment of a secrecy break. Although he dismissed the case as moot due to the CPI's conclusion, Fachin ruled that similar future decisions must be reviewed by two technicians and validated by the Court's presidency. The maneuver involved filing a petition in a previously archived 2021 case to manipulate the judge assignment in favor of Gilmar Mendes.

item.title: Citado em plano para Vorcaro, 'Marcelão' seguirá coordenando comunicação de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Marcelo Lopes, the publicist officially appointed as communications coordinator for Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 campaign, was cited as a strategist in 'Project DV', a plan commissioned by Daniel Vorcaro that involved paying influencers to support the Master Bank and oppose its liquidation ordered by the Central Bank in December 2025. The scheme was first revealed by Malu Gaspar's column and later confirmed in a Folha de S.Paulo report, though the full article remains behind a paywall.

item.title: Governo Lula e Motta fecham acordo para avançar fim da 6 X 1
item.description: The Lula government and Chamber President Hugo Motta have reached an agreement to advance the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule, establishing a maximum 40-hour workweek, two days off per week, and salary maintenance. The text will be voted in a special committee and is expected to reach the plenary in May, followed by a government bill to regulate the change.

item.title: Subvenção do governo evitou alta maior no diesel, diz diretor da ANP
item.description: ANP Director-General Artur Watt stated that the government's diesel subsidy prevented a larger price increase in Brazil despite international market instability caused by the Iran war. He noted that without the subsidy, prices would be closer to U.S. levels, which saw up to 50% increases. While Petrobras, Mataripe, and Vibra have joined the program, distributors like Ipiranga and Raízen remain outside, and payments have not yet been made due to pending agreement with the Federal Revenue.

item.title: O valor doado por família dona da Ypê à campanha de Bolsonaro em 2022
item.description: The family that owns Ypê donated R$ 1.5 million to Jair Bolsonaro’s 2022 presidential campaign in the runoff, with Eduardo Beira as the largest contributor, giving R$ 750 thousand in two transfers. Other family members — Waldir Jr., Antônio Ricardo, and Ana Maria Beira — each donated R$ 250 thousand. The contributions were made by individuals, as corporate donations to political campaigns are prohibited under Brazilian electoral law.

item.title: PT elogia discurso de Nunes Marques no TSE e aposta em eleição sem sobressaltos
item.description: PT members praised the speech of Kassio Nunes Marques, the new president of the TSE, during his inauguration, expressing relief over the expectation of a smooth 2026 election. The positive assessment reflects the party's confidence in his impartiality and the stability of the electoral process under his leadership.

item.title: ‘Bolha que apoia governo é contrária ao agronegócio’, diz presidente da FPA
item.description: FPA president Pedro Lupion claims the Lula government is speaking only to its own 'bubble' and that the agribusiness sector is being 'punished' due to ideological conflict. He cites daily attacks via decrees and ordinances, stressing the need for a strong Harvest Plan and rural debt renegotiation amid a 'perfect storm' of high input costs, low commodity prices, expensive credit, and 20% real interest rates. Lupion supports Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy and states the agro caucus will endorse a right-wing candidate after July party conventions.

item.title: Entenda o que muda com o fim da “taxa das blusinhas”
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional measure eliminating the 20% import tax on international purchases up to US$50, known as the 'blusinhas tax', valid for up to 120 days. The move aims to counter negative public perception among lower-income classes, after the tax was labeled the government's biggest mistake in a recent poll. State-level ICMS tax still applies, with rates ranging from 17% to 20%.

item.title: Independentes e mulheres impulsionam reação de Lula, mas cenário eleitoral segue acirrado com Flávio
item.description: Lula's government approval rose from 43% to 46%, driven by independents and women, cutting the negative approval gap from -9 to -3 points. In the electoral scenario, Lula leads Flávio Bolsonaro 42% to 41% in a technical tie within the margin of error. The improvement is linked to stronger support among independent and female voters, according to Quaest analysts.

item.title: Governo Lula renega, mas fez acordo com Centrão para aprovar taxa das blusinhas
item.description: The Lula government negotiated with the Centrão to approve the 'blusinhas' tax, despite publicly renouncing the import tax on purchases under $50. The deal was exposed in plenary by Deputy José Guimarães (PT-CE), the government leader in the Chamber. The measure, criticized for affecting consumers of cheap imported goods, was defended by the government as necessary for revenue.

item.title: Fim da ‘taxa das blusinhas’ já era calculado pelo varejo de moda em análise eleitoral
item.description: The repeal of the 'blusinhas tax,' an import duty on purchases under $50, was anticipated by fashion retailers as a political risk in an election year. Abvtex had warned in February that the measure could be reversed due to opposition pressure, prioritizing Lula’s re-election over fiscal revenue. Retailers and industry groups criticized the decision, arguing it advantages foreign platforms and harms Brazilian micro and small businesses.

item.title: Sabesp e Comgás vão custear mudança e reconstrução de casas após explosão em São Paulo
item.description: Following the explosion in Jaguaré, West Zone of São Paulo, the state government announced that Sabesp and Comgás will fund the reconstruction or relocation of affected families' homes, offering options such as on-site reconstruction, social rental, or transfer to CDHU properties. Around 40 housing units are ready to accommodate displaced residents, and the R$5,000 emergency aid paid to 84 families is also funded by the concessionaires. Five residences have been definitively interdicted and will be demolished for reconstruction, while the causes of the blast remain under investigation by the companies, IPT, and Civil Defense.

item.title: Quaest: maioria vê Lula 'amigável' com Trump e reunião boa para o Brasil
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released today shows that most respondents viewed the meeting between Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and U.S. President Donald Trump, held on Thursday (7), positively. Interviewees described the encounter as friendly and beneficial for Brazil.

item.title: Oposição não vai atrapalhar plano de segurança, diz Wellington Lima
item.description: Justice Minister Wellington Lima stated that the relationship between government and opposition will not interfere with the Brazil Against Organized Crime program, launched by President Lula with an R$ 11 billion investment. He said the initiative aims to ensure security agents fulfill their duties and will not be politicized or influenced by political noise. The program consists of four pillars: financial strangulation, weapons trafficking and circulation, prison system containment, and forensic investigation and crime resolution.

item.title: Indústria: Fiesp e CNI criticam MP que acaba com "taxa das blusinhas"
item.description: Fiesp and CNI criticized the Provisional Measure that ends the 'blusinhas tax', arguing that the exemption of taxes on international purchases up to US$50 creates unfair competition, harms national industry, and benefits foreign producers, especially from China. The entities state that the measure destroys jobs and sabotages the Brazilian economy.

item.title: Desconforto de Lula e Alcolumbre chama atenção em posse no TSE
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre appeared visibly uncomfortable during the inauguration of Kassio Nunes Marques at the TSE, signaling ongoing tension between them following legislative defeats to the government. Their strained relationship worsened after Alcolumbre personally led the defeat of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination and supported overturning Lula’s veto on the Dosimetry Bill. Despite the rift, Lula’s allies believe he will avoid escalating the conflict, hoping for future rapprochement to prevent interference with priority executive proposals in Congress.

item.title: Crusoé: Eleitor não acredita na moderação de Lula e Flávio, aponta Quaest
item.description: Brazilian voters doubt the moderation of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ahead of the 2026 presidential election, according to a Genial/Quaest poll. 45% of respondents believe Lula is not more moderate than the PT, while 40% think he is. The survey indicates widespread skepticism about either candidate’s ability to distance themselves from their parties’ ideological bases.

item.title: Fim da taxa das blusinhas opõe varejo nacional e importadores; veja argumentos a favor e contra
item.description: President Lula's administration repealed the 'blusinhas tax,' which imposed a 20% import duty on international online purchases under $50, while keeping the Remessa Conforme compliance program. The move sparked a national debate: domestic retailers and manufacturers argue the tax was needed to level the playing field against foreign e-commerce platforms, while importers and consumers welcome its removal as a reduction in living costs. However, ten Brazilian states continue to apply a 20% ICMS on such purchases, preserving part of the tax burden.

item.title: Trump: o melhor cabo eleitoral de Lula
item.description: The meeting between Lula and Donald Trump contributed to a slight improvement in Lula’s personal and government approval ratings, according to Quaest polling, with a 3 to 4-point recovery over the last two weeks. Lula gained traction across all income and education levels, including traditionally unfavorable groups like evangelicals and voters in the South and Center-West, and tied with Flávio Bolsonaro in the pivotal Southeast region. Approval for the Desenrola 2 policy and the ban on betting for the indebted also boosted his image, outweighing negative news such as the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias.

item.title: Para chefão do PT, pesquisas ainda não captaram efeito Trump e Messias
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva says recent polls have not yet captured the positive effects of Lula’s meeting with Donald Trump and the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination, which Lula’s allies believe will boost him electorally. In the Genial/Quaest poll released this week, Lula stands at 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 41% in a second-round simulation, technically tied after Bolsonaro’s son led in April. Edinho Silva notes most voters are not yet focused on the October elections.

item.title: "Não tenho rabo preso", diz Salles em batalha contra Nunes e Centrão. Veja vídeo
item.description: Deputy Ricardo Salles (Novo) rebutted criticisms from São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB), claiming he 'has no tail tied' and can speak freely, while accusing the Centrão of being 'Brazil's cancer' and allied with the PT. Salles rejected the Centrão's support for André do Prado's Senate bid, stating that Nunes' MDB is a base of Lula's government. Nunes, in turn, accused Salles of narcissism and individualism, saying he only creates confusion and that his electoral success depended solely on Bolsonaro's backing.
